overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation on any of three allegations: emailed links shared for a future meeting, the pre-title-change deliberation claim, and missing OML materials for a new member.

allegations.summary: A member emailed all committee members social media links with 'to be discussed tomorrow', allegedly deliberating outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we do not find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law when one of its members shared links to social media templates to be discussed at the Committee’s next meeting.

allegations.summary: Alleged deliberation among members before a committee member changed the Facebook group title, with no specific date or participants identified.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we do not find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: A new member said she never received Open Meeting Law determinations on taking office, yet certified receipt; the committee was alleged to be responsible.
allegations.key_passage: Because the responsibility of providing the materials falls on the municipal clerk, and the Committee itself is not directly responsible for providing these materials to new public body members, we do not find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law with respect to this allegation.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
